description: The two claim classes, stored apart. The general-primer cases here are synthetic: this is the public repository, and it carries the contract and its validator rather than licensed decklists. The engine-closed case here binds a synthetic closure the gate builds, so the five damage tests run without any licensed data; the engine-closed cases for real decks live in the private overlay with the closures they bind, and are not part of a public clone.

expectations: The primer names the deck's curve and where it wants to be on turn three.
The primer describes the plan for contesting Battlefields, without claiming an outcome.
The primer says which slots it could not read, rather than passing over them.
general_primer_cases.notes: Structure and plan only. No coverage claim belongs here even when the deck happens to be closed.

expectations: The primer identifies the deck as reactive and names what it is holding up.
The primer explains the Rune curve in terms of what it can pay for and when.
The primer states that the main deck is short of the required count.
The primer still produces a plan for the cards that are present.
general_primer_cases.notes: A decklist that does not satisfy deck construction still gets a primer; that is what 'any decklist' means.
